Overall market environment 
The Thai economy in 2025 is expected to continue expanding at a subdued pace, with growth projected 
at around 2.0%. Key drags stem from  (1) a slowdown in the tourism sector, as tourist arrivals are expected to 
decline to approximately 33.0 million from 35.1 million in the previous year, reflecting weaker Chinese arrivals amid 
safety concerns and intensified regional competition. (2) Industrial production continues to face headwinds from a 
sustained erosion of competitiveness across key manufacturing segment s, despite some support to  electronics 
production from front-loaded exports to the US ahead of reciprocal tariff announcements. (3) Private consumption 
remains under pressure, particularly in durable goods, due to an ongoing contraction in bank credit.   
During 2025, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) cut policy interest rates throughout the year, resulting 
in the policy rate being lowered to 1.25% by the end of December 2025, in response to slowing economic activity 
and inflation, as well as tighter fina ncial conditions.  The tightening has been particularly pronounced for small 
businesses and low-income households, which face higher vulnerability and more severe pressures, reflected in a 
sharp contraction in SME lending. In addition, inflation remained ne gative for nine consecutive months in 2025, 
resulting in full-year inflation of -0.14%, underscoring persistent weakness in domestic economic conditions. 
In 2026, Thailand’s economic recovery is expected to remain fragile and slow further from 2025, with 
growth projected to stay below potential at around 1.6% before gradually improving in the following year. The 
economy continues to face several key headwinds: (1) elevated household debt and sluggish income recovery are 
constraining commercial bank lending, further weighing on durable goods consumption, particularly automobiles 
and housing; (2) the manufacturing sector is likely to come under renewed pressur e from a slowdown in exports 
following front-loaded shipments ahead of US import tariff hikes in the previous year, with the electronics sector 
particularly vulnerable after earlier export acceleration; and (3) the tourism sector’s contribution to growth i s 
diminishing as tourist arrivals return closer to normal levels, while growth in tourism-related businesses is expected 
to slow significantly compared with the post -COVID recovery phase. Headline and core inflation are projected to 
remain below the Bank of Thailand’s target range, driven by declining global energy prices and persistently weak 
domestic demand amid the slow economic recovery. Low inflation, sub-potential growth, and continued contraction 
in commercial bank credit are expected to prompt the B ank of Thailand to further ease monetary policy, with the 
policy rate projected to be cut to 1.0%. 
Key downside risks to Thailand’s economic outlook in 2026 include: (1) a continued contraction in 
commercial bank credit alongside an acceleration in non-performing loans, which would heighten risks to financial 
stability and significantly weigh on domesti c durable goods consumption; (2) risks stemming from U.S. trade 
policies under President Donald Trump, as sharper import tariff hikes or stricter enforcement of transshipment rules 
could adversely affect global trade volumes and Thailand’s export performance; (3) domestic political uncertainty, 
where disruptions to fiscal policy implementation or delays in government spending could undermine consumption 
and overall economic activity; and (4) a deeper contraction in industrial production due to worsening 
competitiveness and intensifying competition from Chinese products entering the domestic market. 
Domestic auto sales in the first eleven months showed a modest increase of 5. 3% compared to the 
previous year amid fragile economy. The key driver was the increase in passenger car segment led by electric and 
hybrid vehicles sales. Meanwhile sales of commercial vehicles contracted pressured by income and the economic 
slowdown. The second-hand car market also faced challenges in 2025 due to economic slowdown and intensified 
price competition from Chinese automakers.

3 
 
The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) Index continued its decline for the fourth consecutive year, 
reflecting structural challenges facing the Thai economy, including diminishing long -term growth potential, 
heightened political uncertainty, fiscal policies focused on short -term consumption stimulus with a low fiscal 
multiplier, and a monetary policy stance that remains tighter than warranted.  By the end of 2025, the SET Index 
declined by 10.0% to close at 1,259.67 points, down from 1,400.21 points at the end  of 2024. The average daily 
trading value on the SET and MAI (Market for Alternative Investment) markets in 2025 stood at Baht 41,045 million, 
representing a further decline of 11.8% from Baht 46,551 million in 2024. 
Strategic Collaboration with Goldman Sachs Asset Management 
In alignment with the Bank’s strategic direction to strengthen and expand its core business pillars, 
Kiatnakin Phatra Financial Group (KKP) entered into a strategic collaboration with Goldman Sachs Asset 
Management during 2 025. This partnership is intended to broaden global investment opportunities for Thai 
investors, whereby Goldman Sachs Asset Management will provide investment advisory services in multi -asset 
strategies exclusively to KKP in Thailand, subject to the terms of the relevant agreement.  This collaboration marks 
a significant step forward in KKP’s ongoing efforts to enhance its wealth management capabilities and reflects 
Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s long-term commitment to growing its third-party wealth business. As part of 
the collaboration, Goldman Sachs Asset Management will provide KKP with investment advisory services through 
model portfolios in multi-asset strategies.  In addition, KKP will gain access to Goldman Sachs Asset Management’s 
global market insights and benefit from regular knowledge sharing between the two firms. 
The collaboration with Goldman Sachs Asset Management will elevate KKP’s ability to deliver world-class, 
globally diversified portfolios tailored to the evolving needs of Thai investors. By combining Goldman Sachs Asset 
Management’s global investment capab ilities with KKP’s local knowledge, the partnership aims to provide 
differentiated opportunities to investors in Thailand.   
Operating results of the Bank and subsidiaries for the year 2025 and for 4Q25 
For the year 2025 , driven by the Bank’s continued commitment to prudent credit quality management, 
overall asset quality has improved to a well -controlled level. At the same time, the Bank continued to execute its 
strategic initiatives to expand and diversify its business por tfolio, resulting in broader revenue contribution across 
multiple business lines. Consequently, Kiatnakin Phatra Bank and its subsidiaries delivered solid performance  for 
the year 2025 with total net profit of Baht 5,913 million, an increase of 17.5% from 2024, and total comprehensive 
income of Baht 6,504 million, up 24.2% YoY. 
The increase in net profit was primarily attributable to a significant reduction in losses from the sale of 
repossessed vehicles, alongside a decline in expected credit losses, compared with the prior year. In addition, 
overall performance strengthened as the Bank continued to implement its strategic initiatives aimed at broadening 
revenue sources and increasing the contribution of non -interest income, resulting in a YoY strong increase in 
non-interest income. The g rowth in non -interest income helped mitigate the impact from lower interest income, 
which declined following the Bank’s measures to moderate loan growth during the period. 
In 2025, non-interest income increased 18.2% YoY, mainly driven by strong growth in wealth management 
business, contributions from the Dime! business, asset management business, bancassurance fee, and gains on 
financial instruments measured at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL) in line with market conditions. Kiatnakin 
Phatra Securities continued to maintain its position as the No. 1 securities brokerage firm in the market, with a

market share1 of 22.18% for 2025.  These positive drivers helped to alleviate the decline in net interest income of 
13.1% YoY , which continued to soften  and largely reflected slower loan growth under the Bank’s asset 
quality-focused strategy emphasizing higher-quality lending, as well as narrower interest spreads aligned with the 
declining interest-rate environment throughout 2025 and impact from customer support measures.  At the same 
time, effective funding cost management amid slower loan expansion and declining interest rates helped reduce 
the Bank’s overall funding costs. 
As of the end of 2025, total loans declined by 6.7% YoY, consistent with the Bank’s focus on prioritizing 
asset quality. Credit quality remained well controlled, with a reduction in the amount of non-performing loans. The 
non-performing loan (NPL)2 ratio stood at 4.3% as of the end of 2025. Losses from the sale of repossessed vehicles 
also declined significantly as the repossessed-car situations continued to improve. The Bank continued to adopt a 
prudent approach in maintaining an appropriate level of provisions. Total expected credit loss (ECL) provisioning 
for 2025 amounted to Baht 3,693 million, which include additional management overlay to address potential risks 
stemming from ongoing economic uncertainties that may affect asset quality, particularly among customers under 
various relief programs.

For 2025, net interest income amounted to Baht 17,257 million, a decrease of 13.1% YoY. The decline was 
mainly attributable to a 13.8% contraction in interest income, driven by slower loan growth in line with the Bank’s 
asset-quality-focused lending measures, which prioritized high-quality loan segments amid economic uncertainty. 
Additionally, interest income also declined due to the reduction in lending rates following cuts in the policy rate  
throughout 2025, as well as impacts from customer assistance provided under the “Khun Soo, Rao Chuay” support 
program. Meanwhile, interest expenses decreased by 15.3% YoY, reflecting effective and ongoing funding cost 
management together with the downward trend in market interest rates. As a result, the Bank’s loan spread  
declined to 4.5% in 2025, compared with 4.8% in 2024. 
For 4Q25, net interest income totaled Baht 4,266 million, representing a decline of 8.3% YoY. The decrease 
was primarily driven by the contraction in loans, in line with the Bank’s asset quality management measures that 
emphasize high-quality loan origination. Meanwhile, loan spread decreased to 4.5%, compared with 4.6% YoY,

For 2025, non-interest income totaled  Baht 8,217 million, representing a solid increase of 18.2% YoY. 
The growth was driven by both net fee and service income and other operating income. Net fee and service income 
increased 10.0% YoY, mainly supported by higher contributions from the wealth management business, the Dime! 
business, asset management business  in line with the growth in asset under advise, asset under platform, and 
asset under management, as well as higher bancassurance fee. Meanwhile, income from investment banking 
business declined due to market conditions that were less conducive to deal activity.   Kiatnakin Phatra Securities 
continued to maintain its No. 1 market share in securities brokerage, recording a market share4  of 22.18% in 2025. 
Meanwhile, other operating income also increased, primarily from higher gains on financial instruments measured 
at fair value through profit or loss (FVTPL) reflecting favorable market conditions, as well as an increase in income 
related to contributions received from the Financial Institutions Development Fund (FIDF) under the “Khun Soo, 
Rao Chuay” customer assistance program.  
For 4Q25, non-interest income amounted to Baht 2,337 million, an increase of 8.0% YoY. The increase 
was driven by higher net fee and service income from the wealth management business, the Dime! business, asset 
management business, and bancassurance fee, partially offset by lower investment banking income compared to 
4Q24. Other operating income also increased, mainly due to contributions from the FIDF related to customer relief 
measures.

For 2025, the Bank exercised discipline in cost management, leading to a reduction in total operating 
expenses to Baht 14,330 million, representing a 13.2% YoY decrease . In particular,  losses from the sale of 
repossessed vehicles, declined to Baht 2,401 million, a substantial reduction of 50.3% YoY, in line with the 
continued decline in repossessed-car volumes. Other expenses remained well controlled.  Excluding items related 
to foreclosed assets, the cost-to-income ratio for 2025 stood at 46.4%, compared with 44.0% in 2024. 
For 4Q25, operating expenses amounted to Baht 3,620 million, a decrease of 11.0% YoY, primarily due 
to a considerable decline in losses from the sale of repossessed vehicles compared with the same period last year. 
Other operating expenses remained well managed. Excluding items related to foreclosed assets, the 
cost-to-income ratio for 4Q25 was 45.8%, compared with 43.9% in the same quarter of 2024.

For 2025, the Bank maintained a prudent provisioning framework, employing the expected credit loss 
(ECL) model with a comprehensive assessment of a broad range of risk factors. This included an evaluation of the 
potential effects of prolonged economic uncertainty on overall credit quality.  For the year 2025,  the expected credit 
losses amounted to Baht 3,693 million, a decline of 7.1% YoY. The amount also includes additional management 
overlay provisions to proactively address potential risks from the ongoing economic uncertainties, which may 
impact asset quality, particularly among customers participating in the “Khun Soo, Rao Chuay” relief program  as

8 
 
well as customers affected by the flood situation in the southern region.  The combined credit cost, which includes 
both expected credit losses and losses from the sale of repossessed vehicles  for the year 2025 , was 1.72% of 
average loans, remaining well below the Bank’s target range and down from 2.30% in 2024. This improvement 
reflects the effectiveness of the Bank’s ongoing credit quality management measures, which have helped maintain 
overall asset quality at a well -controlled level.  Additionally, the lower provisions were in line with the slowdown in 
loan volume. 
For 4Q25, expected credit loss amounted to Baht 708 million, representing a decline of 22.5% from the 
same period last year. This amount includes additional consideration for the management overlay to accommodate 
potential future risks arising from the still -uncertain economic environment, which may affect credit quality. It also 
accounts for customers participating in various relief programs, including the “Khun Soo , Rao Chuay” scheme, as 
well as customers affected by the flood situation in the southern region.  The expected credit loss and losses from 
the sale of repossessed vehicles (credit cost) for 4Q25 amounted to 1.41% of average loans, improving from 2.18% 
in 4Q24.

Liabilities and Shareholder’s Equity 
As of 31 December 2025, the Bank reported total liabilities on a consolidated basis of Baht 422,889 million, 
representing a  2.8% decrease from end of  2024. Both  deposits and debt issued and borrowings continued to 
decline, in line with the strategic moderation in loan growth. The composition of deposits consisted of  46.8% in 
current and savings accounts,  increasing from 34.5% level at the end of 2024  and 53.2% in term deposits. 
The loan-to-deposit and borrowing ratio stood at 94.4% at the end of 2025. 
Shareholders’ equity attributable to owners of the Bank as of the end of 2025 totaled Baht 64,772 million, 
an increase of 3.0% from the end of 2024. The increase is largely due to the net profit of the Bank’s equity holders 
and offset by the dividend payment made during 2025.

Capital Adequacy Ratio  
The Group maintains a strong capital position and can adequately withstand the current uncertainties and 
is above the regulatory requirement (regulatory requirement and additional capital conservation buffer) of 11.0% 
for total capital ratio, 8.5% for Tier 1 capital and 7.0% for Common Equity Tier 1 capital. The Group performs capital 
management planning to maintain an appropriate level of capital which is consistent with the annual business plan 
of the Group including reviews during the year to ensure appropriate level of capital to withstand any uncertainties. 
As of December 31, 2025, the Capital Adequacy Ratio (BIS ratio) under Basel III which included profit up 
to end of 2024 after dividend payment was at 16.43% while Tier 1 ratio was at 13.67%. When including net profit 
up to end of 4Q25 after interim dividend payment, the BIS ratio will increase to 17.65% while Tier 1 ratio will be 
14.89%. The Bank’s Tier 1 capital are all Common Equity Tier 1, contributing to  83.19% of total capital reflecting 
high quality of capital.

ESG trends and their impact on the Company’s performance 
In 2025, the sustainability landscape and related regulations, both globally and domestically, have become 
increasingly stringent, with a stronger focus on enhancing sustainability disclosures, allocating capital to support 
the transition, and managing sus tainability related risks. These trends are reflected in countries’ heightened 
commitments to addressing climate change. Thailand’s updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0 
sets out the national target toward achieving net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, alongside capital market 
developments that encourage listed companies to strengthen sustainability disclosures, and the ongoing 
development of the Thailand Taxonomy as a reference framework for classifying economic activities from an 
environmental perspective. These developments may have implications for financing decisions involving high 
carbon businesses and for risk management within the financial sector. 
Under this context, Kiatnakin Phatra Financial Group has continued to monitor and study sustainability 
developments, while reviewing relevant regulations and guidelines to integrate sustainability considerations across 
the Group’s operations. This includes setting Group-level sustainability policies, expanding the scope of ESG risk 
assessments for corporate lending clients, providing financing to support customers through the transition, and 
developing financial products and services aligned with the shift toward a low -carbon economy. In addition, 
sustainability and ESG considerations have been incorporated into the process of developing and reviewing the 
Group’s business plan to support effective risk management and long-term sustainable growth.
